title: Verify native game-art request cancellation ordering
classification: Confirmed evidence gap; no handler defect reproduced.

cause.test_fixture: The native admin image route fixture used retired uid:fingerprint session identities after persistent-session enforcement was enabled. Requests were redirected to an unmounted /login route, and TestClient followed the redirect to 404 before handlers ran.
cause.application_behavior: The route runs synchronous image and database work through run_image_work_in_threadpool. Cancellation is deferred until the worker returns, keeping request-scoped database access open until the worker finishes.

change.fixture: Mark the route fixture TESTING so its legacy synthetic identity is accepted by the explicit test-only auth path.
change.regression: Cancel an authenticated native game-art ASGI request while its worker is blocked. Assert cancellation remains pending, then release the worker and verify it completes before the database scope exits.

verification.result: 25 passed on Python 3.12.16 with pinned requirements-dev.txt dependencies.
coverage: The route-level regression uses an authenticated ASGI request and a gated worker, not a real client disconnect.
Separate R1995 tests cover filesystem and database replacement failure ordering.

limits: Cancellation after the worker commits can leave the upload successful while the caller receives no response; this is an ambiguous client outcome, not a rollback guarantee.
No PostgreSQL or real image filesystem mutation was performed by this route cancellation regression.
Representative NAS peak-memory measurements and cancellation-under-load qualification remain open for P0-11.
